content: 1. Estradiol and Fezolinetant: Estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased fezolinetant exposure. 2. Estradiol and Anastrozole: Estradiol reduces the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated as estradiol may diminish the pharmacologic action of anastrozole. 3. Estradiol and Antithrombin Alfa/Antithrombin III: Estradiol decreases the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III via pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Estradiol and Apalutamide: Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects and adjust the dose as needed. 5. Estradiol and Argatroban/Bemiparin/Bivalirudin: Estradiol reduces the effects of these anticoagulants through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Estradiol and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Estradiol and Cimetidine: Cimetidine increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Estradiol and Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Estradiol and Dalteparin/Enoxaparin: Estradiol reduces the effects of these anticoagulants via pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Estradiol and Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Estradiol and Erdafitinib: Erdafitinib increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours. 12. Estradiol and Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Erythromycin increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Estradiol and Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects. 14. Estradiol and Fondaparinux: Estradiol reduces the effects of fondaparinux via pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Estradiol and Givosiran: Givosiran increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of CYP1A2 substrates as clinically appropriate. 16. Estradiol and Heparin: Estradiol reduces the effects of heparin via pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Estradiol and Idelalisib: Idelalisib increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Estradiol and Ivosidenib: Ivosidenib decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 19. Estradiol and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Estradiol and Pacritinib: Estradiol decreases pacritinib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Estradiol and Phenindione/Protamine: Estradiol reduces the effects of these anticoagulants via pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Estradiol and Quinidine: Quinidine increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Estradiol and Rifabutin/Rifampin: These drugs decrease estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Estradiol and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Estradiol and Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates. 26. Estradiol and Albiglutide: Estradiol may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 27. Estradiol and Amikacin/Amoxicillin/Azithromycin: These antibiotics may reduce estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of estradiol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Estradiol and Amiodarone: Amiodarone increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 29. Estradiol and Amobarbital/Butabarbital/Butalbital: These drugs decrease estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Estradiol and Aprepitant: Aprepitant increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Estradiol and Artemether/Lumefantrine: These drugs decrease estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Estradiol and Atazanavir: Atazanavir may increase or decrease estradiol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 33. Estradiol and Atorvastatin: Atorvastatin increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 34. Estradiol and Aztreonam: Aztreonam decreases estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of estradiol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Estradiol and Belzutifan: Belzutifan decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of CYP3A4 substrates. 36. Estradiol and Bosentan: Bosentan decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Estradiol and Bosutinib: Bosutinib increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 38. Estradiol and Budesonide: Budesonide decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Estradiol and Cannabidiol: Cannabidiol may induce or inhibit CYP1A2 metabolism, affecting estradiol levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP1A2 substrates as clinically appropriate. 40. Estradiol and Cephalosporins (e.g., Cefaclor, Cefadroxil, Cefamandole, Cefazolin, Cefixime, Cefpirome, Cefprozil, Ceftazidime, Ceftibuten, Cephalexin): These antibiotics may reduce estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of estradiol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Estradiol and Ceritinib: Ceritinib increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Estradiol and Chloramphenicol: Chloramphenicol increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential side effects. 43. Estradiol and Chlorhexidine Oral: Chlorhexidine oral reduces estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of estradiol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Estradiol and Ciprofloxacin: Ciprofloxacin reduces estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of estradiol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Estradiol and Clindamycin: Clindamycin reduces estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of estradiol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Estradiol and Clotrimazole: Clotrimazole reduces estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 47. Estradiol and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Estradiol and Cortisone: Cortisone decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Estradiol and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Crofelemer is minimally absorbed and unlikely to cause systemic inhibition. 50. Estradiol and Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 51. Estradiol and Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Estradiol and Dapsone: Dapsone reduces estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of estradiol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Estradiol and Darifenacin: Darifenacin increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Estradiol and Darunavir: Darunavir increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
